why_trail.why: Ruling binds Option A: retirement MOVES episodes/active/<id>.md -> episodes/retired/<id>.md, and retired/ is an ARCHIVE, not a second live search space. The seams already implement BOTH adapters behind _LAYOUT_ADAPTER, so binding is deleting the switch and the Option-B branch at six layout-dependent functions. Real risk: ~10 existing tests hardcode the flat path self.root/'<id>.md' and will break; those are path-literal edits, not restructuring. The silent-omission class RELOCATES rather than vanishes -- three new traps (missed subdir glob, forgotten union, stray flat-path file incl episodes/README.md) each need a fixture.

Option A bound at ACTIVE_DIR/RETIRED_DIR in one seam block; _LAYOUT_ADAPTER and both _LAYOUT_OPTION_* deleted. Added a fourth layout concern the seam table did not name: stray_episode_paths() -- a file at the flat root belongs to NEITHER set, so both enumerations would omit it. Surfacing it (raise) rather than skipping it also protects the writer's id-assignment scan from minting an id a stray already holds. commit() gained a compensating rollback because binding A gave placement a SECOND step (write retired/, remove active/) whose failure would leave the id in both directories -- exactly the half-retired store C6 rules out. 18 existing tests needed path-literal updates (not restructuring); two Option-B scaffolding tests were replaced by bound-behavior equivalents. 71 passed, 1 skipped.

Placeholders are README.md rather than .gitkeep (my call, logged): the g1 hazard needs any tracked file, but each directory also has a real thing to say -- active/ that membership is a filesystem fact, retired/ that it is an archive with a named, deliberate way in. A .gitkeep would carry the git property and none of the meaning. Named-not-globbed exclusion: NON_EPISODE_FILENAMES holds README.md, so a stray episode at the flat root is a visible refusal rather than a file that quietly matches nobody's glob. git add -An dry-run lists all three READMEs; check-ignore exits 1 for both new dirs.

Archive is OPT-IN, not opt-out: include_retired defaults False on every SCANNING primitive (enumerate/select/neighbours) and does not exist on fetch, because a lookup by id is not a search and a consolidated-into cross-ref would dangle otherwise. That default is the ruling's second half made mechanical -- an opt-out default would turn every future caller's forgotten filter into a silent correctness bug. Section 7's redundant scan-then-confirm is kept but re-justified: with the layout bound the filter cannot subtract, so its value is now cross-checking two INDEPENDENT seams; a disagreement RAISES (HalfRetiredStore) instead of dropping the id, since dropping is precisely how a candidate set gets quietly short. Envelope now carries include_retired so a consumer cannot mistake an archive-excluding answer for a complete one. 78 passed.

A fixture that passes on day one proves nothing about the trap it names, so each naive implementation was substituted INTO the seam it would occupy and the fixture observed failing -- all five red. Trap 3 turned out to be the one with real teeth beyond retrieval: a stray at the flat path also poisons the writer's id-assignment scan (it would mint an id the stray already holds), so the refusal lives in iter_episode_ids where both the reader and the writer inherit it. The README exclusion is asserted through the ALLOWLIST, not through the answer -- emptying NON_EPISODE_FILENAMES turns the very same file into a stray, which is what proves the exclusion is deliberate. 84 passed.

Two independent defenses, because they cover different failure classes. (1) By construction: the retired CONTENT is only ever rendered to the archive path, so 'fields updated but file not moved' has no representation in the write plan -- asserted against write_plan() directly, not inferred from effects. (2) By compensation: binding A gave placement a SECOND step, so commit() now snapshots the prior bytes of everything it will disturb and, on any failure, restores them and deletes what it newly created. Faults injected at BOTH steps (_place, _remove_superseded), and the source-removal test asserts the archived file was already placed -- proving the injection landed in the gap rather than before it. Honest residual: a hard kill runs no compensation, so that state is made LOUD (half-retired refusal at the enumeration seam, inherited by reader and writer alike) rather than claimed impossible. 89 passed.

C5 green first try, which is itself the finding: the anchor of neighbours() is fetched BY ID, so an archived episode can still walk back to its live cluster -- the move #308 actually needs -- without any retirement-aware special case. That falls out of fetch-by-id being exempt from the archive default (a lookup is not a search), a choice made at m3 for a different reason. Four assertions cover the door in both directions: survivors findable ordinarily, the retired member reachable three ways (by id, by history-inclusive scan, from a survivor's neighbourhood), and a wholly-consolidated cluster empty to search and intact in history. 93 passed.

Section 7 now records the ruling verbatim, states the archive principle as the mechanism (include_retired defaults False), keeps Option B as rejected-with-reason -- explicitly BECAUSE a reader finding four adapters and no record of the second candidate would judge the indirection unearned -- and names the three relocated traps so the next reader does not have to rediscover that binding A moved the failure class rather than killing it. Sections 8/10 now describe what ships rather than what was planned; 10 became built/not-built. Section 9's 'identical file content' is corrected to same content + same blob OID with working-tree bytes platform-dependent (.gitattributes * text=auto, #319), and the test that pins it is cited so doc and test now agree in tone. Also swept the stale Option-B-for-concreteness disclaimers out of ss1/2/3, which the handoff did not list but which would have contradicted the ruling on the first page a reader hits. 93 passed.

All four Required Evidence items produced with pasted output, plus both confirmatory items. Full suite 1251 passed / 3 skipped (episode store 67 -> 93); the three rejection fixtures still exit 1 and are byte-untouched; check-ignore exits 1 for every target and git add -An proves both new READMEs enter the index (the g1 empty-directory hazard is closed, but they are UNTRACKED until the integrator commits -- called out explicitly at the end of the result). Result written with VERDICT: COMPLETE, five-point Workflow Feedback, and Map Impact carrying the ratified decision anchors forward. Not committed.
